instructions.note: The agent is instructed to deploy or migrate production 'using the engineer's credentials,' inheriting the engineer's full personal access token rather than a credential scoped to the specific requested action.

'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy' is a behavioral instruction that removes the one checkpoint capable of catching a mistaken, ambiguous, or malicious instruction before an irreversible production migration executes. No structural approval gate exists to back it up.

controls.name: On-call-only SSO channel restriction
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat channel's identity layer, outside the model, so it does not decay with model capability alone. It is only partially dependent because a new integration surface (ticketing bot, alert webhook, additional channel) could admit requests from outside the on-call SSO population, reclassifying the effective input source from trusted to internal or untrusted without any change to the agent's own behavior.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging occurs at the cloud platform layer, outside agent control, so it does not decay with model capability. However, it attributes every action to the engineer's identity rather than a distinct agent identity, which limits its value for non-repudiation regardless of model strength.

controls.name: Human approval gate with raw action review before irreversible production actions
controls.decay_rationale: A structural, independent gate requiring a named human to review the exact migration or deployment target before execution would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege, action-scoped, short-lived agent credential
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped only to the named deploy or migrate action, issued to the agent rather than borrowed from the engineer's general-purpose personal access token, does not widen regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Distinct, non-forgeable agent identity in audit records
controls.decay_rationale: Recording actions under a service identity bound to the agent, separate from the human requester, resolves repudiation independent of model capability.

controls.name: Immutable retention of chat transcripts for the compliance period
controls.decay_rationale: Retention enforced outside the requesting engineer's control (so the engineer cannot delete the only record of intent) does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: No approval gate on irreversible production database migration executed with a broad delegated credential

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer sends a chat instruction naming a service or migration.

Agent runs the named production migration immediately using the engineer's broad personal access token; prompt.md:3 explicitly forbids asking for confirmation first. Migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: System prompt instructs the agent never to ask for confirmation before deploying or migrating, removing the one checkpoint that could catch a mistaken or ambiguous instruction before an irreversible action runs.

The agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token to act in production, so cap.db_migrate and cap.prod_deploy execute with broad, unscoped privilege rather than a least-privilege, action-specific credential.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making cap.db_migrate an irreversible sink.
No step or runtime limits on unattended agent action are described, so the autonomy modifier is applied conservatively.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review (exact migration script and target shown, not a summary) before any production database migration executes.
Issue the agent a short-lived, action-scoped credential limited to the named deploy or migrate target instead of passing through the engineer's full personal access token.

forecast.watch_signal: A new integration surface (ticketing system, monitoring/alert webhook, or additional chat channel) that can send deploy or migrate requests to the agent without the current SSO-authenticated, on-call-only restriction, or any documented broadening of who or what may issue such requests.

findings.title: Shared personal credential and deletable transcript defeat non-repudiation of agent-executed production actions

attack_path.note: Engineer issues an instruction to deploy or migrate.
Agent executes using the engineer's token; the cloud audit log (store.cloud_audit_log) records the action under the engineer's name, not a distinct agent identity.
Same attribution gap applies to deployments.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name because the agent acts using the engineer's personal access token; there is no distinct agent identity in the log.

The chat transcript is the only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted, and engineers can delete their own chat history, so the one artifact that could distinguish an agent-initiated action from a manual one, or establish intent, can be destroyed by the same person the action is attributed to.
Because migrations are irreversible, a disputed or mistaken action cannot be undone, and without independent attribution there is no reliable way to reconstruct who or what caused it.

recommendations.action: Attribute agent-initiated actions to a distinct service identity in the cloud audit log, separate from the requesting engineer's identity.
Make chat transcripts immutable and non-deletable by the requesting engineer for the compliance retention period, so the record of intent cannot be unilaterally erased.

forecast.watch_signal: Same signal as f1: any new path for requests to reach the agent outside the on-call SSO channel. If the attribution gap persists while the trusted-only assumption erodes, an unattributable irreversible action could originate from a source the design never accounted for.

rating.rationale: Both findings run the same trusted-source (T) instruction through an execute capability classified S3 (cap.db_migrate is irreversible; both capabilities use a broad, unscoped delegated credential), giving a base inherent tier of moderate under the rubric's T-to-S3 cell, raised to high by the autonomy modifier because no step or runtime limits are declared. No credited preventive control exists: the system prompt explicitly forbids confirmation, the credential is broad rather than least-privilege, and the only structural controls present (the on-call-only SSO restriction and cloud audit logging) are either not covering the sink (access restriction only constrains who can speak to the agent, not what the agent does once addressed) or purely detective (audit logging, which gets no tier credit and is itself undermined by attributing actions to the engineer rather than the agent). Residual therefore equals inherent at high. The forecast turns on ctrl.access_restriction: it is the only control currently keeping the input source classified as trusted (T) rather than internal or untrusted (I/U). Under data_scope_expansion or intended_purpose_change (new integration surfaces such as ticketing bots or alert webhooks), that control is defeated, the source reclassifies toward U, and the U-to-S3 cell is critical even before the autonomy modifier. The single control whose erosion moves the forecast the most is ctrl.access_restriction.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live system, IAM policy document, or audit log sample was reviewed.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not specified in the provided artifacts and were treated as unset, which conservatively triggers the rubric's autonomy modifier.

Credential scope was inferred as 'broad' because the design states the agent uses the engineer's personal access token directly rather than an agent-specific scoped credential; the actual IAM permissions attached to that token were not provided, so confidence on exact blast radius is medium.

The on-call-only SSO access restriction is described only in documentation and was not independently verified against an access control configuration, so ctrl.access_restriction is recorded as 'declared' rather than 'verified'.
